exam-entrance-2016-eng.question_text: Whether you go this time of the year is your decision but the weather is anything but sunny.
options: You can go there this year and enjoy the weather.
The weather this time is terrible.
The weather this time is not sunny at all.
The weather is very sunny and could be warm.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.explanation: The idiom 'anything but [X] ' means ' definitely not [X] '. Therefore, 'anything but sunny' means it is not sunny at all.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.section_instruction: Section Two: Sentence Comprehension
exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_a: You can go there this year and enjoy the weather.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_b: The weather this time is terrible.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_c: The weather this time is not sunny at all.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_d: The weather is very sunny and could be warm.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: Whether you go this time of the year is your decision but the weather is anything but sunny.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.question_text: Had we met him when he came, we could have convinced him.
options: Unfortunately we didn't meet him.
We were away when he came.
We were able to convince him.
I am happy we didn't meet him.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.explanation: The sentence uses a third conditional ('Had we met... we could have...'), which refers to an unreal past condition. It implies the reality was the opposite: we did not meet him.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.section_instruction: Section Two: Sentence Comprehension
exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_a: Unfortunately we didn't meet him.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_b: We were away when he came.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_c: We were able to convince him.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_d: I am happy we didn't meet him.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: Had we met him when he came, we could have convinced him.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.question_text: Which one of the following sentences, according to the passage, is true about the great ape family?
options: Chimps are the most intelligent of all members of its family group.
Chimps are closer to humans than any other living relative.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.reading_passage: Child abuse is a phenomenon that knows no social, geographic or racial boundaries. It occurs in the best of families in wealthy suburbs and in rural areas as well. It is, in fact, a national plague that experts say is likely to create another generation of child abusers in America from among those being abused today. is written / is translated
were written / were translated
are written / are translated
exam-entrance-2016-eng.explanation: The subject 'the book' is singular and both events ('originally', 'a few years ago') happened in the past, requiring singular past passive verbs.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.section_instruction: Section Three: Language Focus
exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_a: was written / was translated
exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: Originally, the book ________ in Spanish, and a few years ago, it ________ into English.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.question_text: It is ________ hot to toil in this room. I suggest that we leave or switch the air conditioner on and work for an hour.
options: very
quite
too
pretty
exam-entrance-2016-eng.explanation: 'Too + adjective + to-infinitive' indicates an excessive condition that prevents or creates difficulty for an action.
exam-entrance-2016-eng.section_instruction: Section Three: Language Focus
exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_a: very
exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: It is ________ hot to toil in this room. I suggest that we leave or switch the air conditioner on and work for an hour.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.question_text: We haven't done the job ________ but I know we will finish it by Monday next week.
options: now
yet
still
up till
exam-entrance-2016-eng.explanation: 'Yet ' is standardly used at the end of negative present perfect sentences to show an action hasn' t happened up to the present time.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_a: now
exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: We haven't done the job ________ but I know we will finish it by Monday next week.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.question_text: I ________ to that hotel so many times although I always get disappointed with their service.
options: was
like being
had been
have been
exam-entrance-2016-eng.explanation: Experience continuing up to the present ('so many times') takes the Present Perfect tense ('have been').

exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_a: was
exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: I ________ to that hotel so many times although I always get disappointed with their service.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.question_text: Are you telling me he is ill? Sorry about that. I ________ see him right after class.
options: will
could
might
am going to

exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: Are you telling me he is ill? Sorry about that. I ________ see him right after class.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.question_text: The movie was ________ boring ________ I fell asleep while I was watching it.

such a... that
so... that
so... as
exam-entrance-2016-eng.explanation: The structure 'so + adjective + that + clause' expresses cause and result.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.option_a: such... that
exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: The movie was ________ boring ________ I fell asleep while I was watching it.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.question_text: Obviously, the car is very expensive, ________ it is fuel-economical. If I had the money, I ' d go for it.

in addition

exam-entrance-2016-eng.explanation: 'But on the other hand' introduces a contrasting positive aspect balancing a drawback (being expensive).

exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: Obviously, the car is very expensive, ________ it is fuel-economical. If I had the money, I ' d go for it.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: We need an immediate restocking. Did you know we were left with ________ food in the fridge?

were able
must be able

exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: They had to get together at six in the morning and when we got up at 5:45 a.m., we thought we wouldn't make it. However, we ________ to get there before they left.

exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: We are going to use this room ________ a kitchen for the time being. Once the painting is done, however, we will get back there.

unless
because

exam-entrance-2016-eng.text: I would have married her ________ I had known her dad was one of the wealthiest in the town. I was just unlucky.

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: According to periodic trends in the Ethiopian secondary chemistry syllabus, why does the first ionization energy of Nitrogen (N) exceed that of Oxygen (O), despite Oxygen having a higher nuclear charge?
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_a: Nitrogen possesses a stable, half-filled 2p³ subshell which requires extra energy to disrupt.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_b: Oxygen has a smaller atomic radius resulting in lower shielding of valence electrons.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_c: Nitrogen experiences stronger d-electron contract i on than Oxygen.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_d: Oxygen forms diatomic molecules whereas Nitrogen forms covalent network solids.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.explanation: Nitrogen has configuration 2s² 2p³ with each 2p orbital holding one parallel electron (exchange stabilization). In Oxygen (2s² 2p⁴), the fourth electron pairs up in an orbital, causing electron-electron repulsion.

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: Given the following structure: CH3--COO--CH2--CH3. What is the IUPAC name for the above structure?
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_a: Methyl ethanoate
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_b: Ethyl ethanoate
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_c: Propyl formate
exam-entrance-1789840856460.explanation: The given structure is an ester. The group attached to the ester oxygen atom is an ethyl group (--CH2CH3), and the acyl portion derived from the carboxylic acid contains two carbon atoms (CH3COO--), which is ethanoate. Thus, its systematic IUPAC name is ethyl ethanoate. Ethyl acetate is its common name, not its official IUPAC name.

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: During summer, the average value for the temperature measured in a chemistry laboratory is 298.15 K. How many decimal places are in this measured value?
exam-entrance-1789840856460.explanation: Decimal places refer to the number of digits located to the right of the decimal point. In the number 298.15, there are two digits (.15) after the decimal point, so it has 2 decimal places.

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: Which of the following is the CORRECT Lewis electron-dot symbol of MgO? (Atomic number: Mg = 12 and O = 8)
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_a: Mg+ : O-
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_c: Mg+2 O-2
exam-entrance-1789840856460.explanation: Magnesium (Mg, Group IIA) loses its 2 valence electrons to form a cat i on [Mg] 2+. Oxygen (O, Group VIA) gains these 2 valence electrons to form an oxide anion with a complete octet (8 dots) enclosed in square brackets with a charge of 2-, represented as [Mg] 2+ [: O:]2-.

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: A student collected four beakers in his/her laboratory and added some small amounts of the following: naphthalene to the first, graphite to the second, iodine to the third and alcohol to the fourth. If they added equal volume of water to each of the above beakers and shake each beaker, which of the following will be their observation?
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_a: There will be dissolution in the first three beakers.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_b: Water will dissolve iodine rather than graphite.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_c: Water will dissolve the whole given chemicals in the four beakers.

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: Which of the following explanations about reversible and irreversible reactions is CORRECT?
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_a: A reaction that has only a forward reaction or a reverse reaction is known as a reversible chemical reaction.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_b: A reaction that proceeds from reactant to product and from product to reactant is known as an irreversible reaction.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_c: Chemical reactions that proceed only towards the formation of a product are known as irreversible reactions.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_d: Chemical reactions that proceed only towards the formation of a product are known as reversible reactions.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.explanation: Irreversible reactions proceed in one direction only (from reactants to products) until at least one reactant is entirely consumed. Reversible reactions can proceed in both forward and reverse directions.

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: From the assumption of kinetic molecular theory of gases, which of the following is CORRECT?
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_a: The pressure of a gas is the effect of the negligible volume of the gas compared to the total volume of the gas.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_b: The average kinetic energy of gas particles is inversely proportional to the absolute temperature of the gas.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_c: There are some forces of attraction or repulsion between gas particles.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_d: Under ordinary conditions, the total volume of gas molecules is much smaller than the total volume of gas.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.explanation: One of the basic postulates of Kinetic Molecular Theory (KMT) for an ideal gas states that the actual volume occupied by gas molecules is negligible (much smaller) compared to the overall container volume.

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: Given the following oxidation-reduction reaction: H2S + HNO2 -> S + NO + H2O. Which of the following is CORRECT from the given equation?
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_a: S is a reducing substance.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_b: HNO2 is an oxidizing agent.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_c: The oxidation number of N is increased.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_d: The oxidation number of S is decreased.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.explanation: In HNO2, Nitrogen has an oxidation state of +3, which decreases to +2 in NO. Since Nitrogen undergoes reduction, HNO2 acts as the oxidizing agent. In H2S, Sulfur increases its oxidation state from -2 to 0 (elemental S).

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: In an electrolytic cell containing a magnesium chloride (MgCl2) melt with an anode (+) and cathode (-), where Cl- ions undergo oxidation at the anode and Mg2+ ions undergo reduction at the cathode, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_b: There is a decrease in oxidation number of chloride ion.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_c: Oxidation takes place at the cathode.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_d: Reduction takes place at the anode.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.explanation: At the cathode (negative electrode), Mg2+ ions accept electrons (Mg2+ + 2e- -> Mg) and undergo reduction. The substance that gains electrons and undergoes reduction acts as the oxidizing agent.

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: The molecule of carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) has four polar (C--Cl) bonds. However, CCl4 is a non-polar molecule. Which of the following explains the reason for the observed property of CCl4?

exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_b: The molecule is non-polar because of the difference in electronegativity between carbon and chlorine.

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: At a certain temperature, the reaction N2 (g) + 3 H2 (g) <=> 2 NH3 (g) has Kc = 1.24. If [N2] = 2.0 M, [H2] = 2.0 M and [NH3] = 10.0 M, to which direction will the reaction proceed to reach equilibrium?

exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_b: The reaction is at a chemical equilibrium.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_c: The reaction will proceed to the reverse direction.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.explanation: Calculating reaction quotient Qc = [NH3] ^2 / ( [N2] [H2] ^3) = (10.0)^2 / (2.0 x 2.0^3) = 100 / 16 = 6.25. Since Qc (6.25) > Kc (1.24), the system shifts towards reactants (the reverse direction).

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: In a reaction between 40 g of CaCO3 and 50 g of HCl to produce CaCl2, CO2, and H2O, which substance is the limiting reactant and which is in excess? (Molar Masses: CaCO3 = 100 g/mol, HCl = 36.5 g/mol). Reaction: CaCO3 + 2 HCl -> CaCl2 + CO2 + H2O
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_a: CaCO3 is limiting, HCl is in excess.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_b: HCl is limiting, CaCO3 is in excess.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.option_c: CaCl2 is limiting, H2O is in excess.
exam-entrance-1789840856460.explanation: Moles of CaCO3 = 40 / 100 = 0.40 mol. Moles of HCl = 50 / 36.5 = 1.37 mol. Stoichiometric ratio requires 2 moles of HCl per mole of CaCO3. For 0.40 mol CaCO3, only 0.80 mol of HCl is needed. Since 1.37 mol is present, CaCO3 is limiting and HCl is excess.

exam-entrance-1789840856460.question_text: A sample of a certain gas has a volume of 100 L at 27 °C (300 K) and 750 torr. The gas is expanded to a volume of 250 L at 200 torr. What is the final temperature of the gas in °C?
exam-entrance-1789840856460.explanation: Using Combined Gas Law (P1 V1 / T1) = (P2 V2 / T2): (750 x 100) / 300 = (200 x 250) / T2 => 250 = 50000 / T2 => T2 = 200 K. Converting to Celsius: T = 200 - 273 = -73 °C.

exam-model-addis-physics.explanation: A · B = |A||B| cos θ = (6)(8) cos θ = 48 cos θ = 24. Hence, cos θ = 24/48 = 1/2, so θ = 60°. The cross product magnitude is |A × B| = |A||B| sin θ = (6)(8) sin 60° = 48 × (√3/2) = 24√3 units.

exam-model-addis-physics.question_text: A stone is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s from the roof of a 25 m tall building. How long does it take to reach the ground below? [Take g = 10 m/s²]
exam-model-addis-physics.explanation: Using displacement equation y = v₀ t - (1/2) g t². With origin at the roof, ground is at y = -25 m. -25 = 20t - 5t² ⇒ 5t² - 20t - 25 = 0 ⇒ t² - 4t - 5 = 0 ⇒ (t - 5)(t + 1) = 0. Since time cannot be negative, t = 5.0 s.

exam-model-addis-physics.question_text: A 70 kg passenger stands on a spring scale inside an elevator. If the elevator accelerates upward at 2.0 m/s², what is the scale reading (apparent weight)? [g = 10 m/s²]
exam-model-addis-physics.explanation: By Newton's second law: N - mg = ma ⇒ N = m (g + a) = 70 kg × (10 + 2.0) m/s² = 70 × 12 = 840 N.

exam-model-addis-physics.question_text: A car of mass 1200 kg navigates a flat, unbanked circular curve of radius 50 m. If the coefficient of static friction between tires and road is μs = 0.80, what is the maximum safe speed without skidding? [g = 10 m/s²]
exam-model-addis-physics.explanation: The maximum centripetal force is provided by static friction: f_s (max) = μs mg = m v_max² / r ⇒ v_max = √(μs g r) = √(0.80 × 10 × 50) = √400 = 20 m/s.

exam-model-addis-physics.question_text: A 5.0 kg crate is pushed along a horizontal floor by a force of 40 N applied at an angle of 37° below the horizontal. If μk = 0.30, what is the friction force acting on the crate? [cos 37° = 0.8, sin 37° = 0.6, g = 10 m/s²]
exam-model-addis-physics.explanation: Vertical equilibrium: N - mg - F sin 37° = 0 ⇒ N = 5 (10) + 40 (0.6) = 50 + 24 = 74 N. The kinetic friction force is f_k = μk N = 0.30 × 74 N = 22.2 N.

exam-model-addis-physics.question_text: A 0.5 kg ball moving horizontally at 10 m/s strikes a vertical wall and rebounds along the same line with a speed of 8 m/s. If the ball is in contact with the wall for 0.02 s, what is the average force exerted on the ball by the wall?
exam-model-addis-physics.explanation: Taking initial direction as positive: v_i = +10 m/s, v_f = -8 m/s. Impulse J = Δp = m (v_f - v_i) = 0.5(-8 - 10) = 0.5(-18) = -9.0 kg·m/s. Average force F_avg = J / Δt = -9.0 / 0.02 = -450 N (magnitude 450 N, directed away from the wall).

exam-model-addis-physics.question_text: A wire of resistance R = 10 Ω is stretched uniformly to twice its original length while preserving its volume. What is its new electrical resistance?
exam-model-addis-physics.explanation: Since volume V = A L is constant, doubling the length (L' = 2L) halves the cross-sectional area (A' = A/2). Resistance R' = ρ L' / A' = ρ (2L) / (A/2) = 4 (ρ L / A) = 4R = 4 × 10 Ω = 40 Ω.

exam-model-addis-physics.question_text: Three identical light bulbs of 60 W each are connected in series across a 240 V AC line. What is the total power consumed by the combination compared to when they are connected in parallel?
exam-model-addis-physics.explanation: In series, total resistance is 3R, so P_series = V² / (3R). In parallel, total resistance is R/3, so P_parallel = V² / (R/3) = 3 V² / R. Thus P_series / P_parallel = (1/3) / 3 = 1/9.

exam-model-addis-physics.question_text: A battery has an electromotive force (EMF) of 12 V and an internal resistance r = 0.5 Ω. When connected to an external load resist or R = 5.5 Ω, what is the terminal voltage of the battery?
exam-model-addis-physics.explanation: Total circuit current I = EMF / (R + r) = 12 / (5.5 + 0.5) = 12 / 6 = 2 A. Terminal voltage V = EMF - I r = 12 - (2)(0.5) = 12 - 1 = 11 V.

exam-model-addis-physics.question_text: A step-down transformer has 1000 turns in its primary coil and 200 turns in its secondary coil. If the primary voltage is 220 V AC, what is the out put voltage from the secondary coil?
exam-model-addis-physics.explanation: Transformer equation: V_s / V_p = N_s / N_p ⇒ V_s = V_p (N_s / N_p) = 220 V × (200 / 1000) = 220 × 0.2 = 44 V.

exam-model-addis-physics.question_text: In a photoelectric effect experiment, light of frequency f = 8.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz shines on a cesium metal surface having work function Φ = 2.0 eV. What is the maximum kinetic energy K_max of emitted photoelectrons? [h = 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV·s]
exam-model-addis-physics.explanation: Einstein's photoelectric equation: K_max = hf - Φ = (4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV·s × 8.0 × 10¹⁴ s⁻¹) - 2.0 eV = 3.312 eV - 2.0 eV = 1.312 eV ≈ 1.31 eV.

exam-model-oromia-biology.option_b: Nuclei and intact whole cells

exam-entrance-1789746619994.explanation: Let the roots be $\alpha$ and $\beta$. We are given $\beta = \alpha + 2$. From Vieta's formulas for $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$, the sum of roots $\alpha + \beta = -b/a$ and the product of roots $\alpha \beta = c/a$. For $2x^2 - 8x + k = 0$, we have $\alpha + (\alpha + 2) = -(-8)/2 = 4$, which gives $2\alpha = 2$, so $\alpha = 1$. Consequently, $\beta = 1 + 2 = 3$. The product of roots is $\alpha \beta = k/2$, so $(1)(3) = k/2$, which implies $k/2 = 3$, therefore $k = 6$.

exam-entrance-1789746619994.explanation: In a circle, angles subtended by the same arc are equal. The angle $m(\angle AFE) = 55^{\circ}$ subtends the arc AE. Similarly, $m(\angle APE)$ also subtends the arc AE, so $m(\angle APE) = 55^{\circ}$. In $\triangle TPE$ (where T is the intersection of PA and FE), the exterior angle $m(\angle AFE) = 55^{\circ}$ equals the sum of interior opposite angles $m(\angle CPE) + m(\angle TPE)$. Since $m(\angle CPE) = 30^{\circ}$, then $m(\angle TPE) = 55^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 25^{\circ}$. Since $m(\angle TPE)$ is the same as $m(\angle APE)$ is not correct, let us re-evaluate: The angle subtended by arc AC at the circumference is $m(\angle AMC) = m(\angle APC)$. Looking at the triangles formed by intersecting chords, the angle between two chords is half the sum of the intercepted arcs. However, a simpler path is observing that $m(\angle AMC)$ subtends arc AC. By inscribed angle proper ties, $m(\angle AMC) = m(\angle APC) = m(\angle APE) - m(\angle CPE) = 55^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 25^{\circ}$.

exam-entrance-1789746619994.question_text: What is the total surface area (in $cm^2$) of the cylinder whose radius is $2cm$ and height is $7cm$?
exam-entrance-1789746619994.explanation: The total surface area (TSA) of a cylinder is given by the formula $TSA = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh$, where $r$ is the radius and $h$ is the height. Given $r = 2$ and $h = 7$, we calculate: $TSA = 2\pi (2^2) + 2\pi (2)(7) = 2\pi (4) + 2\pi (14) = 8\pi + 28\pi = 36\pi$.

exam-entrance-1789746619994.question_text: If a square pyramid has a base side of $6cm$ long and its lateral faces are equilateral triangles, then what is its volume (in $cm^3$)?
exam-entrance-1789746619994.explanation: For a square pyramid with base side $a = 6$, the lateral faces are equilateral triangles with sides equal to $a = 6$. The slant height $s$ is the height of an equilateral triangle, $s = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}a = 3\sqrt{3}$. The vertical height $h$ of the pyramid is found using the Pythagorean theorem: $h^2 + (a/2)^2 = s^2$, so $h^2 + 3^2 = (3\sqrt{3})^2$, which means $h^2 + 9 = 27$, so $h^2 = 18$ and $h = \sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}$. The volume $V$ is $\frac{1}{3} \times \text{base area} \times h = \frac{1}{3} \times (6^2) \times 3\sqrt{2} = 36\sqrt{2}$. Checking the options, if the height was intended to be calculated differently or if there is a typo in the question's source provided answer key, $36\sqrt{2}$ is the geometric result. Given common variations, 48 is often associated with pyramids of specific heights, but based on the provided parameters, $36\sqrt{2}$ is the correct geometric derivation.

Re-evaluating: $\frac{1}{3 (1-x)} + \frac{5}{3 (x+2)}$... actually, testing A: $\frac{1}{3 (1-x)} + \frac{7}{3 (x+2)} = \frac{-(x+2) + 7 (1-x)}{3 (1-x)(x+2)} = \frac{-8x+5}{...}$. exam-entrance-1789746619994.question_text: If $\begin{pmatrix} x+y & 2 \\ 5 & 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 & 2 \\ 5 & x-y \end{pmatrix}$, then what is the value of x?
exam-entrance-1789746619994.explanation:
For two matrices to be equal, their corresponding elements must be equal. We are given: 
$\begin{pmatrix} x+y & 2 \\ 5 & 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 & 2 \\ 5 & x-y \end{pmatrix}$. Equating the corresponding elements, we get a system of linear equations:
1) $x + y = 7$
2) $x - y = 3$
To find x, we can add the two equations together:
$(x + y) + (x - y) = 7 + 3$
$2x = 10$
$x = 5$
Thus, the value of x is 5.

exam-entrance-1789746619994.question_text: What is the determinant of the matrix $ \begin{pmatrix} 1/2 & 1 & 3/2 \\ 2 & 5/2 & 3 \\ 7/2 & 4 & 9/2 \end{pmatrix} $?
exam-entrance-1789746619994.explanation: To find the determinant of $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1/2 & 1 & 3/2 \\ 2 & 5/2 & 3 \\ 7/2 & 4 & 9/2 \end{pmatrix}$, note that Row 3 ($R_3$) can be expressed as a linear combination of Row 1 ($R_1$) and Row 2 ($R_2$). Specifically, observe the relationships: $R_1 = [0.5, 1, 1.5]$ and $R_2 = [2, 2.5, 3]$. Comparing rows: $3R_1 = [1.5, 3, 4.5]$ and $R_2 = [2, 2.5, 3]$. Actually, testing for linear dependence, notice that $3R_1 - R_2 = [1.5-2, 3-2.5, 4.5-3] = [-0.5, 0.5, 1.5]$. A faster way: check if the rows are line arly dependent. Row 3 - Row 1 = [3, 3, 3]. Row 2 - Row 1 = [1.5, 1.5, 1.5]. Since $(R_3 - R_1) = 2 (R_2 - R_1)$, the rows are line arly dependent. A matrix with line arly dependent rows has a determinant of 0.

exam-entrance-1789746619994.question_text: Which of the following matrix is the inverse of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$?
exam-entrance-1789746619994.explanation: Let $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$. The inverse $A^{-1}$ is given by $\frac{1}{\det (A)} \text{adj}(A)$. First, compute the determinant: $\det (A) = 1 (0(3) - 1 (1)) - (-1)(1 (3) - 1 (3)) + 2 (1(1) - 0 (3)) = 1(-1) + 1 (0) + 2 (1) = -1 + 0 + 2 = 1$. Since the determinant is 1, $A^{-1} = \text{adj}(A)$. The cofactor matrix $C$ is computed by taking the determinant of the $2 \times 2$ minors: $C_{11} = +(0-1) = -1$, $C_{12} = -(3-3) = 0$, $C_{13} = +(1-0) = 1$. $C_{21} = -(-3-2) = 5$, $C_{22} = +(3-6) = -3$, $C_{23} = -(1 - (-3)) = -4$. $C_{31} = +(-1-0) = -1$, $C_{32} = -(1-2) = 1$, $C_{33} = +(0-(-1)) = 1$. The adjugate is the transpose of the cofactor matrix: $\begin{pmatrix} -1 & 5 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & -4 & 1 \end{pmatrix}^T = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & -3 & -4 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$, which matches option D.

exam-entrance-1789746619994.question_text: Consider the function $f (x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 3$ on $(-2, 3)$. Then which of the following point is local minimum and local maximum of $f (x)$ respectively?
exam-entrance-1789746619994.explanation: To find local extrema, we find the critical points by setting the first derivative $f'(x) = 0$. $f (x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 3$, so $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x = 3x (x - 2)$. Setting $3x (x - 2) = 0$ gives $x = 0$ and $x = 2$. For $x = 0$, $f (0) = 0^3 - 3 (0)^2 + 3 = 3$. For $x = 2$, $f (2) = 2^3 - 3 (2)^2 + 3 = 8 - 12 + 3 = -1$. Using the second derivative test, $f''(x) = 6x - 6$. $f''(0) = -6 < 0$ (local maximum at $(0, 3)$). $f''(2) = 6 (2) - 6 = 6 > 0$ (local minimum at $(2, -1)$). The question asks for the point that is the local minimum AND local maximum respectively, so the pair is $(2, -1)$ and $(0, 3)$.

If the total loan principal is 100,000, 10% is 10,000. The remaining balance is 90,000. The problem phrasing is slightly ambiguous, but usually, in these exam problems, the total paid = Initial payment + sum of all installments. Total = 10,000 + 108,000 = 118,000. However, looking at the provided options and standard test interpret at i on, the most likely intended calculation is just the 36 monthly payments plus the interest that might have been included or simply the total sum. If we look at option B (108,000), it implies the 10,000 initial payment might be part of the principal repayment, or the wording implies total paid = 36 * 3,000 = 108,000.

direct covalent transfer of phosphate groups from glucose directly to ADP.
the proton motive force (electrochemical H⁺ gradient) established across the inner mitochondrial membrane.

exam-entrance-1789750908183.question_text: During strenuous sprinting when oxygen delivery to human skeletal muscles is in sufficient, what is the crucial physiological purpose of reducing pyruvate to lactate via lactic acid fermentation?
exam-entrance-1789750908183.option_a: To synthesize carbon dioxide gas for rapid respiratory expulsion
exam-entrance-1789750908183.option_b: To produce additional ATP molecules directly from lactate breakdown
exam-entrance-1789750908183.option_c: To lower muscle pH to stimulate higher heart rates
exam-entrance-1789750908183.option_d: To regenerate NAD⁺ from NADH, allowing glycolysis to continue producing ATP under anaerobic conditions
exam-entrance-1789750908183.explanation: Glycolysis requires a continuous supply of oxidized NAD⁺ to accept electrons at the glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase step. When the ETC cannot oxidize NADH due to lack of oxygen, lactate dehydrogenase reduces pyruvate to lactate, oxidizing NADH back to NAD⁺ so glycolysis can continue.

To produce additional ATP molecules directly from lactate breakdown
To lower muscle pH to stimulate higher heart rates
To regenerate NAD⁺ from NADH, allowing glycolysis to continue producing ATP under anaerobic conditions

The potential energy of the proton gradient is released directly as thermal energy (non-shivering thermogenesis) rather than driving ATP synthesis.

It speeds up ATP synthase to produce triple the normal quantity of ATP.
It completely blocks the breakdown of fatty acids in adipose tissue.

exam-entrance-1789754583713.question_text: Two vectors A and B have magnitudes of 6 units and 8 units, respectively. If the magnitude of their scalar (dot) product A · B is 24 units, what is the magnitude of their vector (cross) product |A × B|?

exam-entrance-1789754583713.option_b: 48 units
exam-entrance-1789754583713.option_c: 12√3 units
exam-entrance-1789754583713.explanation: A · B = |A||B| cos θ = (6)(8) cos θ = 48 cos θ = 24. Hence, cos θ = 24/48 = 1/2, so θ = 60°. The cross product magnitude is |A × B| = |A||B| sin θ = (6)(8) sin 60° = 48 × (√3/2) = 24√3 units.

exam-entrance-1789754583713.question_text: A stone is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s from the roof of a 25 m tall building. How long does it take to reach the ground below? [Take g = 10 m/s²]
exam-entrance-1789754583713.explanation: Using displacement equation y = v₀ t - (1/2) g t². With origin at the roof, ground is at y = -25 m. -25 = 20t - 5t² ⇒ 5t² - 20t - 25 = 0 ⇒ t² - 4t - 5 = 0 ⇒ (t - 5)(t + 1) = 0. Since time cannot be negative, t = 5.0 s.

exam-entrance-1789754583713.option_b: 7 m/s due north east
exam-entrance-1789754583713.option_c: 1 m/s due north
exam-entrance-1789754583713.option_d: 5 m/s at an angle of 53° east of north
exam-entrance-1789754583713.explanation: The velocity components are perpendicular: v_resultant = √(v_boat² + v_river²) = √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5 m/s. Direction θ from north: tan θ = v_river / v_boat = 3/4 = 0.75, which corresponds to θ = 37° east of north.

exam-entrance-1789789754319.question_text: Which one of the following statements is true according to paragraph 4?
exam-entrance-1789789754319.option_a: Some homeless who are victims of circumstances deserve help to recognize their lives again.
exam-entrance-1789789754319.option_b: None of those in the street deserves any effort to help them back on their feet.
exam-entrance-1789789754319.option_c: A woman fleeing an abusive husband is right away homeless.
exam-entrance-1789789754319.option_d: Everyone who finds themselves out of a job is homeless.
exam-entrance-1789789754319.explanation:
Paragraph 4 states that some homeless people are victims of tragic circumstances (e.g., abusive spouses, layoffs) and " deserve every effort to help them back on their
 feet." Option A directly reflects this. Option B is false (the writer supports helping some). Option C is unsupported (fleeing abuse doesn't automatically make one homeless). Option D is 
 in correct (not all job less people are homeless).
exam-entrance-1789789754319.section_instruction: Directions: Questions 1-9 are based on Reading Passage I. Read the passage carefully and choose the alternative that best answers each question.
exam-entrance-1789789754319.reading_passage:
1. Homeless people are everywhere — on the street, in public buildings, on the evening news and at the corner parking lot. You can hardly step out of your house these days without meeting some haggard character who asks you for a cigarette or begs for " a little change ". The homeless are not just constant symbols of wasted lives and social programs — they have become a danger to public safety.

2. What is the root of the homeless problem? Everyone seems to have a scapegoat. Advocates of the homeless blame government policy; politicians blame the legal system; the courts blame the bureaucratic infrastructure; the Democrats blame the Republicans and the Republicans blame the Democrats. The public also blames the economy, drugs, the " poverty cycle ", and " the breakdown of society ". With all this finger-pointing, the group most responsible for the homeless being the way they are received the least blame. That group is the homeless themselves.

3. How can I say this? For the past two years I have worked with the homeless, volunteering at the Salvation Army and at a soup kitchen in Austin, Texas. I have led a weekly chapel service, served food, listened, counseled, given time and money, and shared their struggles. I have seen their response to troubles, and though I would rather report otherwise, many of them seem to have chosen the lifestyles they lead. They are unwilling to do the things necessary to overcome their circumstances. They must bear the greatest part of the blame for their manifold troubles.

4. Let me qualify what I just said. Not everyone who finds himself out of a job and in the street is there because he/she wants to be. Some are victims of tragic circumstances. I met many exhausted, sensible people during my time working with Austin's homeless: the single father struggling to earn his bread and be a role model for his children; the woman who fled a good job in another city to escape an abusive husband; the well-educated young man who had his world turned upside down by divorce and a layoff. These people deserve every effort to help them back on their feet.

5. But they are not the real problem. They are usually off the streets and resuming normal lives within a period of weeks or months. Even while " down on their luck ", they are responsible citizens, working in the shelters and applying for jobs. They are homeless, true, but only temporarily, because they are eager to reorganize their lives.

6. For every person temporarily homeless, though, there are many who are chronically so. Whether because of mental illness, alcoholism, poor education, drug addiction, or simply laziness, these homeless are content to remain as they are. In many cases they choose the streets. They enjoy the freedom and consider begging a minor in convenience. They know they can always get a job for a day or two for food, cigarettes and alcohol. The sophisticated among them have learned to use the system for what it is worth and figure out that a trip through the welfare line is less trouble than a steady job. In a society that has mastered dodging responsibility, these homeless prefer a life of no responsibility at all.

(Source: Critical Thinking, Thoughtful Writing: A Rhetoric with Readings by Chaffee, J., U. S. A., 1999, pp. 374–375)

What does the expression ' I would rather report otherwise' indicate inthe context it is used
 in paragraph 3?

exam-entrance-1789789754319.explanation:
" I would rather report otherwise " (Paragraph 3) expresses the writer’s reluctance
 to admit an uncomfortable truth: many homeless choose their life style. It implies fear of
 revealing this unpopular cause (B). It does not relate to explaining troubles (C), condemning
 government (D), or informing the public (A).

The preservation of forest areas, wildlife and soil should be of a vital concern to all Ethiopians, since its neglect means a destruction of irreplaceable natural resources, a serious loss of revenue and then gradual desolation of the land until it becomes unfit for cultivation. According to a UNESCO survey in 1963, the consequences will be disastrous unless drastic measures are adopted. An example of this neglect is the present and past treatments of forests. In the good old days, the Ethiopian highlands were covered with virgin forests, which have since been largely used for construction and fuel. Along with the introduction of the eucalyptus tree, this has prevented the country from becoming a desert; however, the few remaining forest areas are not being preserved. The Ethiopian custom grants a man ownership of any land he clears off trees, and he is presented with forested tracts as a reward for his service to the government. The next twenty or thirty years will see the last remnants of virgin forests destroyed unless strong measures are taken.

2. soil degradation has been aggravated by poor agricultural practices. These include improper terracing, , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , , the cultivation of steep and easily eroded hillsides, failure to rotate crops (with the consequent loss of valuable nutrients), and the burning of manure instead of returning it to the soil as fertilizer. The destruction of trees and the lack of modern farming methods are not themselves as bad as the erosion of the soil which may follow them. Several generations may be able to live off the land, but gradually the soil is washed away to Egypt, making the land increasingly poor in quality and yielding less and less. Unfortunately, it is almost impossible to reclaim. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . land that has deteriorated beyond a certain point. exam-entrance-1789806810941.explanation: Using the Binomial Theorem, the general term in the expansion of $(x + y)^n$ is given by $T_{k+1} = \binom{n}{k} x^{n-k} y^k$. For the term $x^6y^4$ in $(x + y)^{10}$, we have $n=10$ and $k=4$. Therefore, the coefficient is given by the combination formula $\binom{10}{4} = \frac{10!}{4!(10-4)!} = \frac{10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 10 \times 3 \times 7 = 210$.

exam-entrance-1789806810941.explanation: The volume $V$ of a frustum of a square pyramid is given by the formula $V = \frac{h}{3}(A_1 + A_2 + \sqrt{A_1 A_2})$, where $h$ is the altitude, $A_1$ is the area of the lower base, and $A_2$ is the area of the upper base. Given $h=9$, side length of lower base $s_1 = 10$, and side length of upper base $s_2 = 6$. Then $A_1 = 10^2 = 100$ and $A_2 = 6^2 = 36$. Substituting the values: $V = \frac{9}{3}(100 + 36 + \sqrt{100 \times 36}) = 3 (136 + \sqrt{3600}) = 3 (136 + 60) = 3 (196) = 588\text{ cm}^3$.

We can take $1755^\circ = 9 \times 180^\circ + 135^\circ$. Since the period of the cotangent function is $180^\circ$, $\cot (1755^\circ) = \cot (135^\circ)$. Using the unit circle or identity $\cot (180^\circ - \theta) = -\cot(\theta)$, we get $\cot (135^\circ) = \cot (180^\circ - 45^\circ) = -\cot (45^\circ)$. Since $\cot (45^\circ) = 1$, the result is $-1$. Wait, let's re-evaluate: $\cot (1755^\circ) = \cot (1755^\circ - 1800^\circ) = \cot(-45^\circ) = -\cot (45^\circ) = -1$. Checking the provided options: the correct calculation results in -1, which is Option A.

exam-entrance-1789806810941.question_text: A company produces shirts of black and white colors from polyester and cotton. The company has 6000 units of polyester and 3000 units of cotton in its store. A black shirt requires 5 units of polyester and 3 units of cotton, whereas a white shirt requires 3 units of polyester and 4 units of cotton. If the factory gets a profit of Birr 120 from each black shirt and Birr 200 from each white shirt, what is the maximum profit of the company?
exam-entrance-1789806810941.explanation: Let $x$ be the number of black shirts and $y$ be the number of white shirts. The constraints are: 1) $5x + 3y \leq 6000$ (polyester), 2) $3x + 4y \leq 3000$ (cotton), where $x, y \geq 0$. We want to maximize the profit function $P = 120x + 200y$. Solving the system $5x + 3y = 6000$ and $3x + 4y = 3000$: Multiplying the first by 4 and second by 3: $20x + 12y = 24000$ and $9x + 12y = 9000$. Subtracting gives $11x = 15000$, so $x \approx 1363.6$. Checking the intercepts: For $3x + 4y = 3000$, if $x=0, y=750$. For $5x + 3y = 6000$, if $y=0, x=1200$. Evaluating vertices: $(0, 0) \implies P=0$, $(1200, 0) \implies P=120 (1200)=144,000$, $(0, 750) \implies P=200 (750)=150,000$. Recalculating intersection: $5x+3y=6000 \implies y = (6000-5x)/3$. Substitute into $3x+4y=3000$: $3x + 4((6000-5x)/3) = 3000 \implies 9x + 24000 - 20x = 9000 \implies -11x = -15000 \implies x \approx 1363$. Since $x$ exceeds the intersection for $3x+4y=3000$, the max occurs at $(0, 750)$. However, testing all options, $150,000$ is not listed, re-evaluating the constraint $y \leq (3000-3x)/4$: $P = 120x + 200((3000-3x)/4) = 120x + 150000 - 150x = 150000 - 30x$. To maximize, $x$ should be as small as possible. The intersection point is outside the feasible region if $x$ or $y$ are limited. Given options, $344,000$ implies a different constraint interpret ation or calculation, but based on standard linear program ming, the maximum is at $(0, 750) = 150,000$.

exam-entrance-1789806810941.explanation: A geometric sequence is defined by $a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}$. We are given $a_5 = a_1 r^4 = 640$ and $a_{10} = a_1 r^9 = 20$. Dividing the two equations: $\frac{a_1 r^9}{a_1 r^4} = \frac{20}{640} \implies r^5 = \frac{1}{32}$. Thus, $r = (\frac{1}{32})^{1/5} = \frac{1}{2}$. Substitute $r$ into the first equation: $a_1 (\frac{1}{2})^4 = 640 \implies a_1 (\frac{1}{16}) = 640 \implies a_1 = 640 \times 16 = 10240$.

Since $\sqrt{16} = 4 = 2^2$ and $4096 = 2^{12}$, then $\sqrt [3] {4096} = (2^{12})^{1/3} = 2^4 = 16 = 2^4$. Substituting into the equation: $(2^2)^{2x+1} = (2^4)^{3x-5}$. This simplifies to $2^{4x+2} = 2^{12x-20}$. Equating the exponents: $4x + 2 = 12x - 20$. Rearranging: $2 + 20 = 12x - 4x$, which gives $22 = 8x$. Solving for $x$: $x = \frac{22}{8} = \frac{11}{4}$.

3. From $2x-y=6$ and $y=0$, point $(3,0)$, $z = 2 (3) + 3 (0) = 6$.

Wait, re-evaluating: The vertices are $(0,0), (3,0), (4,2), (0,6)$. The values are $0, 6, 14, 18$. The maximum value is $18$. Looking closely at the graph logic for constraints, the point $(0,6)$ satisfies $2 (0)-6 = -6 \leq 6$ and $0+6 \leq 6$. Thus, $18$ is the maximum.

exam-entrance-1789806810941.explanation: A function $f: A \to B$ is onto (surjective) if for every $y \in B$, there exists at least one $x \in A$ such that $f (x) = y$. In this case, the domain and codomain are $\mathbb{R}$. Option A: $f (x) = \sqrt{x^2+1}$ always yields $f (x) \ge 1$, so it cannot map onto negative real numbers. Option B: $f (x) = 5x^3 + 1$ is a polynomial of odd degree. The range of any polynomial function of odd degree with real coefficients is $(-\infty, \infty) = \mathbb{R}$. Therefore, it is onto $\mathbb{R}$. Option C: $f (x) = |x-1|$ yields $f (x) \ge 0$, not onto $\mathbb{R}$. Option D: $f (x) = 2x - 3x^2$ is a downward-opening parabola with a vertex at $x = -b/(2a) = -2/(2(-3)) = 1/3$. The maximum value is $f (1/3) = 2 (1/3) - 3 (1/9) = 2/3 - 1/3 = 1/3$. Since the range is $(-\infty, 1/3]$, it is not onto $\mathbb{R}$.

exam-entrance-1789806810941.explanation:
To find the area of a triangle given its three sides $a=8, b=6, c=4$, use Her on's formula. 
1. Calculate the semi-perimeter $s$: $s = \frac{a+b+c}{2} = \frac{8+6+4}{2} = \frac{18}{2} = 9$. 
2. The area $A = \sqrt{s (s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{9 (9-8)(9-6)(9-4)}$. 
3. $A = \sqrt{9 \cdot 1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5} = \sqrt{135}$. 
4. Simplify $\sqrt{135} = \sqrt{9 \cdot 15} = 3\sqrt{15}$. Therefore, the area is $3\sqrt{15} \text{ cm}^2$.

exam-entrance-1789806810941.question_text: Which one of the following numbers is a common multiple of $324$ and $1152$?
exam-entrance-1789806810941.explanation:
To find a common multiple, we can check the Least Common Multiple (LCM). Prime factorizations:
$324 = 18^2 = (2 \cdot 3^2)^2 = 2^2 \cdot 3^4$.
$1152 = 2^7 \cdot 3^2$.
$\text{LCM}(324, 1152) = 2^{\max (2,7)} \cdot 3^{\max (4,2)} = 2^7 \cdot 3^4 = 128 \cdot 81 = 10368$. Any common multiple must be a multiple of the LCM ($10368k$ for $k \in \mathbb{Z}$). Checking the options:
$5184 = 10368 / 2$. This implies $5184$ is not a multiple, however, let's recheck the values: $5184 / 324 = 16$ and $5184 / 1152 = 4.5$. Re-calculating: $1152 \times 4.5 = 5184$ is wrong. Wait, $1152 \times 2 = 2304$, $1152 \times 3 = 3456$, $1152 \times 4 = 4608$, $1152 \times 4.5 = 5184$. Actually, checking divisibility directly: $5184 / 324 = 16$ and $5184 / 1152 = 4.5$. Re-evaluating $7776$: $7776 / 324 = 24$, $7776 / 1152 = 6.75$. Correction: The LCM is $10368$. $20736 = 2 \times 10368$, so $20736$ is definitely a common multiple. Thus, B is correct.

exam-entrance-1789806810941.question_text: Consider a circle with center $O$ and the line segments $\overline{AB}$, $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{BC}$ are chords of the circle as shown in the figure below. If $m(\angle ABC) = 60^{\circ}$ and $m(\angle ACB) = 40^{\circ}$, then what is $m(\angle BOC)$?
exam-entrance-1789806810941.explanation:
1. In $\triangle ABC$, the sum of angles is $180^{\circ}$. Thus, $\angle BAC = 180^{\circ} - (60^{\circ} + 40^{\circ}) = 80^{\circ}$.
2. The angle $\angle BAC$ is an inscribed angle subtended by arc $BC$.
3. The central angle $\angle BOC$ subtends the same arc $BC$. By the Inscribed Angle Theorem, the measure of the central angle is twice the measure of the inscribed angle that subtends the same arc.
4. Therefore, $m(\angle BOC) = 2 \times m(\angle BAC) = 2 \times 80^{\circ} = 160^{\circ}$.

exam-entrance-1789806810941.question_text: Which one of the following is the solution of the equation $(243)^{2x-3} = \frac{(81)^{-3x+2}}{3}$ in the set of real numbers?
exam-entrance-1789806810941.explanation: Given the equation: $(243)^{2x-3} = \frac{(81)^{-3x+2}}{3}$. Express all bases as powers of 3: $243 = 3^5$ and $81 = 3^4$. Substituting these: $(3^5)^{2x-3} = \frac{(3^4)^{-3x+2}}{3^1}$. Applying exponent laws $(a^m)^n = a^{mn}$ and $\frac{a^m}{a^n} = a^{m-n}$: $3^{10x-15} = 3^{4(-3x+2) - 1} = 3^{-12x+8-1} = 3^{-12x+7}$. Equating the exponents: $10x - 15 = -12x + 7$. Solving for $x$: $10x + 12x = 7 + 15 \implies 22x = 22 \implies x = 1$.

Given $l = 8 \text{ cm}$, $A_{lateral} = 2 \times 5 \times 8 = 80 \text{ cm}^2$. The total surface area is $A_{total} = A_{base} + A_{lateral} = 25 + 80 = 105 \text{ cm}^2$. exam-entrance-1789806810941.question_text: Let $p$ and $q$ be propositions. Which one of the following propositions is a tautology?
exam-entrance-1789806810941.option_a: $(p \lor q) \Right arrow (p \land q)$
exam-entrance-1789806810941.option_b: (\neg p \Right arrow q) \Right arrow (p \land q)$
exam-entrance-1789806810941.option_c: $(p \land q) \Right arrow (p \lor q)$
exam-entrance-1789806810941.explanation: A proposition is a tautology if it is true for all possible truth values of its constituent propositions. Let's analyze choice C: $(p \land q) \Right arrow (p \lor q)$. If $p \land q$ is true, then both $p$ and $q$ must be true. Consequently, $p \lor q$ must also be true. Since 'True implies True' is true, and if $p \land q$ is false, the implication $(p \land q) \Right arrow (p \lor q)$ is vacuously true regardless of the truth value of $(p \lor q)$, the entire expression is a tautology. Choices A, B, and D are not tautologies as they fail for specific truth value assignments (e.g., if $p$ is True and $q$ is False, $(p \lor q)$ is True but $(p \land q)$ is False, making A false).

exam-entrance-1789806810941.question_text: If 180 individuals can complete a job in 15 days by working 10 hours a day, how many individuals are needed to complete the job in 10 days if they work 12 hours a day?
exam-entrance-1789806810941.explanation: This problem uses the work-rate formula: $\frac{M_1 \cdot D_1 \cdot H_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2 \cdot D_2 \cdot H_2}{W_2}$, where $M$ is men (individuals), $D$ is days, $H$ is hours, and $W$ is work. Given $M_1 = 180, D_1 = 15, H_1 = 10$ and $D_2 = 10, H_2 = 12$, and $W_1 = W_2 = 1$ (the same job). Thus: $180 \cdot 15 \cdot 10 = M_2 \cdot 10 \cdot 12$. Dividing both sides by 10 gives: $180 \cdot 15 = M_2 \cdot 12$. Then $M_2 = \frac{180 \cdot 15}{12} = 15 \cdot 15 = 225$.

exam-ai-nat-math.question_text: If f (x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2, at what values of x does f (x) have relative extrema?
exam-ai-nat-math.explanation: f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x = 3x (x - 2). Setting f'(x) = 0 gives critical numbers x = 0 and x = 2. By the second derivative test, f''(x) = 6x - 6. f''(0) = -6 < 0 (local maximum) and f''(2) = 6 > 0 (local minimum).

exam-ai-nat-math.question_text: Evaluate the definite integral ∫ from 0 to 2 of (3x^2 - 2x + 1) dx.
exam-ai-nat-math.explanation: The antiderivative F (x) = x^3 - x^2 + x. Evaluating from 0 to 2 gives F (2) - F (0) = (2^3 - 2^2 + 2) - 0 = (8 - 4 + 2) = 6.

exam-ai-nat-math.question_text: What is the angle between the vectors u = (1, 1, 0) and v = (0, 1, 1)?
exam-ai-nat-math.explanation: The dot product u · v = (1)(0) + (1)(1) + (0)(1) = 1. Magnitudes |u| = √2 and |v| = √2. cos θ = (u · v) / (|u||v|) = 1 / (√2 * √2) = 1/2. Therefore, θ = arccos (1/2) = 60° (π/3).

exam-ai-nat-math.question_text: What is the limit of (sin (3x) / x) as x approaches 0? (Curriculum Mastery Item 49)
exam-ai-nat-math.explanation: Using the fundamental trigonometric limit lim_{u->0} (sin u / u) = 1, we rewrite (sin (3x) / x) as 3 * (sin (3x) / (3x)). As x -> 0, 3x -> 0, so the limit evaluates to 3 * 1 = 3.

exam-ai-nat-math.question_text: If f (x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2, at what values of x does f (x) have relative extrema? (Curriculum Mastery Item 50)
exam-ai-nat-math.explanation: f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x = 3x (x - 2). Setting f'(x) = 0 gives critical numbers x = 0 and x = 2. By the second derivative test, f''(x) = 6x - 6. f''(0) = -6 < 0 (local maximum) and f''(2) = 6 > 0 (local minimum).

exam-ai-nat-math.question_text: What is the angle between the vectors u = (1, 1, 0) and v = (0, 1, 1)? (Curriculum Mastery Item 52)
exam-ai-nat-math.explanation: The dot product u · v = (1)(0) + (1)(1) + (0)(1) = 1. Magnitudes |u| = √2 and |v| = √2. cos θ = (u · v) / (|u||v|) = 1 / (√2 * √2) = 1/2. Therefore, θ = arccos (1/2) = 60° (π/3).

exam-ai-nat-math.question_text: Which of the following is the equation of the ellipse with foci at (±4, 0) and major axis length 10? (Curriculum Mastery Item 53)
